title: Food groups and what they do
examples: If I eat too much sugar, what happens to my energy?
Which nutrient helps my bones to stay strong?
Do I need to drink water even if I eat lots of fruit?

explain.say: Today we say about the different food groups we eat.

draw.text: Food groups and what they do

explain.say: Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: a healthy plate. Look at the vegetables, the fruit and the grains. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

draw.text: Food groups and what they do

explain.say: Carbohydrates give you quick energy to play and learn all day.
Protein is like the building blocks for your muscles and hair.
Fats are important because they help keep your body warm and store energy.
Vitamins and minerals are like tiny helpers that keep your body working right.

items: Vitamin C helps keep your gums healthy.
Calcium (a mineral) is needed for strong bones.
Iron (a mineral) helps carry oxygen in blood.

explain.say: Fibre, found in plants, helps your digestive system move smoothly.

faq.q: Why do I need to eat different food groups every day?
faq.a: Your body needs different nutrients for different jobs. For example, you need protein to build muscles and carbs for energy.
asks: What is the purpose of eating a balanced diet?
Why can't I just eat only one type of food?

faq.q: Is it true that fats are always bad for me?
faq.a: Not all fats are bad. Healthy fats, like those in nuts, are important for absorbing vitamins and keeping you warm.
asks: What kind of fats should I eat more of?

faq.q: What is the difference between vitamins and minerals?
faq.a: Vitamins are organic compounds your body needs, like Vitamin C. Minerals are inorganic elements, like calcium, that come from the earth.
asks: Are vitamins and minerals the same thing?
Where do I get my minerals from?

faq.q: Does drinking water count as getting nutrients?
faq.a: Water itself does not have nutrients, but it is vital for carrying nutrients around your body and helping you digest food.
asks: Why do I need to drink so much water?

faq.q: If I eat a lot of sweets, will I get enough energy?
faq.a: You will get quick energy from sweets, which are mainly carbohydrates. However, you will miss out on the building materials from protein and fats.
asks: What happens if I only eat sugary snacks?

facts: Carbohydrates are the body's main source of immediate energy.
Protein is essential for growth and repair of tissues.
Minerals like calcium are crucial for strong bones and teeth.
Fibre helps to keep the digestive system working correctly.
Water is necessary for all chemical reactions in the body.

quiz.say: Which nutrient group provides the main source of quick energy for playing?
quiz.why: Carbohydrates are broken down into glucose, which the body uses immediately for energy.

wrong.1: Protein is mainly used for building and repairing tissues, not quick energy.
wrong.2: Fats store energy for later use, but carbohydrates provide the quickest fuel.
wrong.3: Vitamins are helpers; they do not provide the main source of energy.

quiz.say: If a student has weak bones, which mineral should they focus on getting enough of?
quiz.why: Calcium is the key mineral needed by the body to build and maintain strong bones.

wrong.0: Iron is more related to carrying oxygen in the blood, not bone structure.
wrong.1: Vitamin C helps absorb minerals, but calcium is the mineral needed for the bones themselves.
wrong.2: Fibre is for digestion, not for building the hard structure of bones.

quiz.say: A person who eats only bread and pasta will lack which nutrient group for long-term energy and warmth?
quiz.why: Fats are vital for long-term energy storage and keeping the body insulated when it is cold.

wrong.0: Carbohydrates are good for quick energy, but they do not store energy as effectively as fats.
wrong.1: Water is for processes, but it does not provide stored energy reserves.
wrong.3: Protein is needed for building, not primarily for long-term energy storage.
